subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: When a spit grows across a bay, joining two headlands and trapping a lagoon behind it, it forms a:
questions.explain: A bar forms where a spit extends across a bay, often enclosing a lagoon.

questions.q: Large boulders piled at the base of a cliff to absorb wave energy are called:
questions.explain: Rock armour is large boulders placed at the cliff foot to absorb and break wave energy.

questions.q: On a coast with alternating hard and soft rock, resistant rock tends to form ____ and softer rock forms ____.
questions.explain: Resistant rock juts out as headlands while softer rock is eroded back into bays.

options: Allowing low-value land to flood and the coastline to move back
questions.explain: Managed retreat lets the sea flood low-value land, creating natural defences like salt marsh.

questions.q: The coastal erosion process where waves throw pebbles against a cliff, wearing it away, is:
questions.explain: Abrasion occurs as waves hurl sediment against the cliff, grinding it away.

questions.q: Groynes are wooden or rock barriers built out into the sea in order to:
options: Trap sediment and build up the beach
questions.explain: Groynes interrupt longshore drift, trapping sediment to widen the beach.

questions.q: Beach nourishment is an example of:
questions.explain: Beach nourishment, adding sand or shingle, is a soft engineering approach.

questions.q: A long ridge of sand or shingle joined to the land at one end and projecting into the sea is a:
questions.explain: A spit is a depositional ridge attached to the coast at one end, formed by longshore drift.

questions.q: Constructive waves are best described as:
options: Low, gentle waves with a strong swash that build up beaches
High, frequent waves with a strong backwash that erode beaches
Waves that only occur in storms
Waves that flow inland as rivers
questions.explain: Constructive waves have a strong swash and weak backwash, depositing material to build beaches.

options: Have a strong backwash that removes material and erodes the coast
questions.explain: Destructive waves have a strong backwash and steep, frequent form, eroding the coast.

questions.q: A wave-cut platform is formed as:
options: A stack collapses into a stump
A cliff retreats, leaving a rocky surface at its base
Sediment is deposited at a river mouth
questions.explain: As waves undercut and the cliff retreats, a flat rocky platform is left at the base.

questions.q: Longshore drift is the process that:
options: Transports sediment ALONG the coast in a zig-zag motion
questions.explain: Longshore drift moves sediment along the coast as swash arrives at an angle and backwash returns straight down.
